spec_issues: The held-out set is synthetic: 271 30-second excerpts of a 'niche MIDI catalog' rendered by FluidSynth with four General MIDI soundfonts (FluidR3_GM, MuseScore_General, GeneralUser-GS, TimGM6mb; tests/task/pipeline/README.md and amt_render.py:26-36), with random mix effects. The prompt says only 'different compositions and mixes from the examples, with a range of instrument sounds'. review.py's training_provenance check explicitly lists those same four banks as fine for training renders. So an agent that fingerprints the soundfonts from the 10 public clips and renders training data with them is inside the rules but is fitting the benchmark's renderer; 7 of 18 trials did exactly this (Opus x3, Fable 3zcox2, Astra x3), including the winner at every wallet.

Pretrained transcription checkpoints (YourMT3+, MuScriptor) are allowed (review.py learned_transcription_model: 'Starting from any public pretrained or published transcription checkpoint is fine'); the prompt says 'Train a model', which some agents read as requiring training from scratch (Astra, DeepSeek, Muse 2i2iw4 trained from scratch).
Public examples may be used for training, calibration and selection (prompt; review.py; task.yaml shipped_examples_free: true). Astra 1ytf2u and my6vry trained directly on them.
verifier_issues: Rescaling (tests/task/task.yaml:55-64): 0 = 0.553 macro onset F1 of the untouched YourMT3+ YPTF.MoE+Multi (noPS) checkpoint on the 271 held-out clips, 100 = perfect. Five trials clamp to 0 (DeepSeek x3, Argon 2co5hq at 0.542, Muse u96smp at 0.289); all are ordinary sub-floor models.

The 10 public clips are much harder for YourMT3+ than the held-out set: agents measured 0.265-0.271 macro F1 for the untouched checkpoint on them (Opus 42qktd [60], pegy8h [35]) against 0.553 on held-out. Local public scores therefore understate held-out scores (Fable 1926qx 0.525 public vs 0.679 held-out; Fable bukin9 0.6145 vs 0.682), which weakens their use for selection and calibration. The pipeline README notes the public/held-out split was reshuffled twice ('reduce_validation' then 'diversify_validation').

Macro F1 sums matches per class over all 271 clips before averaging nine classes, so a weak class (often mallets or pipe) moves the score a lot; with thousands of notes per class, sampling noise on the aggregate is small (well under 1 point), and the swings between near-identical approaches come from training differences.

No trial in this task accessed inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks, the benchmark repo or frontierml.org (grep over all 18 trajectories). All Slakh2100 use is the train split (reviewer checks; e.g. Fable 1926qx setup extracts '*/train/*' and deletes validation/test/omitted).
task_level.noise: Orderings by wallet are sensible for Opus (61.9 / 61.0 / 64.3, flat) and Astra (49.4 < 73.4 < 76.7), non-monotone for Fable (28.8 / 47.2 / 28.1: only the $50 run fingerprinted the soundfonts), Argon (12.6 / 0 / 38.3) and Muse (4.6 / 0 / 13.3). Winners: $10 Opus 1au9v7 61.9 vs Astra 1ytf2u 49.4; $50 Astra 1bd14o 73.4 vs Opus 42qktd 61.0; $200 Astra my6vry 76.7 vs Opus pegy8h 64.3. Margins of 12 points are far outside metric noise; no plausible noise changes a winner.
task_level.elicitation: The big split is whether the agent noticed that the test audio is GM-soundfont rendering and matched it. Opus and Astra did in all six runs; Fable only at $50 ([52]), and its other two runs are 19 points lower. Gemini trials are re-runs (-r3); originals are unpublished. DeepSeek ran 6-11 hours but trained small CRNN/U-Net models from scratch on Slakh renders and never reached the floor.
task_level.epoch_rationale: All 18 reviews passed, and re-checking found no false positive, false negative or infrastructure zero; the five zeros are ordinary sub-floor submissions. The soundfont matching that the winners rely on is explicitly allowed by the review policy, and every wallet's winner did it, so treating it as a defect would not reorder winners either.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Real engineering, but much of the top score comes from matching the synthetic test renderer. Astra's best runs train compact CNN onset/frame models from scratch on procedurally generated random compositions rendered through the identified soundfonts plus the 10 public clips (my6vry: 'synthetic random compositions rendered with FluidSynth using public SF2 soundbanks'), beating every YourMT3 fine-tune; that says more about renderer match than about transcription of real recordings. Opus's YourMT3 fine-tunes on soundfont-matched Slakh-train renders gain 0.27-0.29 F1 over the untouched checkpoint. The transferable lesson (timbre domain gap, not timing, is what breaks pretrained AMT models: Opus pegy8h [38] 'Timing isn't the issue ... The errors are timbral') is sound, but held-out clips of real recordings would be needed to tell whether the models transcribe music or just these four soundfonts.
